sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LITTLE CHANGE IN THE UPPER PATTERN IS FORECAST THIS PERIOD....WITH TROUGHING TO REMAIN OVER THE EAST...AND RIDGING OVER THE S CENTRAL AND SWRN STATES. AT THE SURFACE...A WEAK FRONT IS FORECAST TO CROSS THE NORTHEAST/MID-ATLANTIC DURING THE AFTERNOON IN CONJUNCTION WITH AN ASSOCIATED MID-LEVEL FEATURE. MEANWHILE...A FRONT SHIFTING SWD ACROSS THE RED RIVER VALLEY REGION/SRN PLAINS AND WWD ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS SHOULD BECOME MORE WELL-DEFINED WITH TIME...AS HIGH PRESSURE SHIFTS SEWD OUT OF CANADA AND INTO THE N CENTRAL U.S. THROUGH THE PERIOD.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS AND VICINITY
sections.text: SELY FLOW TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE SURFACE FRONT LYING ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS BENEATH 35 TO 45 KT WLYS AT MID-LEVELS WILL RESULT IN FAVORABLE SHEAR FOR ORGANIZATION OF STORMS EXPECTED TO BE DEVELOPING OVER THE HIGH PLAINS BY AFTERNOON. FUELED BY A DESTABILIZING AIRMASS...INITIAL CONVECTION IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP INVOF SERN WY -- AIDED BY UPSLOPE FLOW. STORMS SHOULD BECOME SUPERCELLULAR GIVEN AFOREMENTIONED SHEAR...WITH THREATS FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS LIKELY WITH STRONGER CELLS. IN ADDITION...DEGREE OF LOW-LEVEL VEERING/SHEAR IS SUPPORTIVE OF ISOLATED TORNADO POTENTIAL. WITH TIME...STORMS SHOULD CONSOLIDATE/MERGE INTO AT LEAST A FEW CLUSTERS...WHICH WOULD THEN MOVE SEWD TOWARD THE LOWER PLAINS -- PARTICULARLY INTO THE EVENING AS SELY LOW-LEVEL JET INCREASES ACROSS THE AREA. SEVERE THREAT SHOULD CONTINUE THROUGH THE EVENING AND LINGER INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS...THOUGH SOME DECREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY IS EXPECTED AFTER MIDNIGHT.

sections.title: THE SOUTHEAST
sections.text: SHORT-WAVE TROUGH SHIFTING ESEWD ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST COMBINED WITH MOIST/DESTABILIZING AFTERNOON AIRMASS SHOULD FUEL WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT. MODERATE WLYS/WNWLYS ALOFT SHOULD SUPPORT FAIRLY FAST-MOVING STORM CLUSTERS...AND ASSOCIATED/LOCAL WIND DAMAGE POTENTIAL. THREAT SHOULD MAXIMIZE IN LATE AFTERNOON...DIMINISHING DURING THE EVENING WITH THE LOSS OF DIURNALLY-MORE-FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMICS.

sections.title: THE NORTHEAST
sections.text: SHORT-WAVE TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED/WEAK COLD FRONT MOVING ACROSS THE UPPER OH VALLEY INTO NY/PA AND THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION SHOULD SUPPORT PERSISTENT CONVECTION...BUT ALSO WIDESPREAD CLOUD COVER WHICH SHOULD HINDER DESTABILIZATION POTENTIAL ACROSS THIS REGION. WHILE SOME POCKETS OF GREATER HEATING/DESTABILIZATION WILL LIKELY SUPPORT CLUSTERS OF MORE ROBUST STORMS -- AIDED BY MODERATE FLOW ALOFT...OVERALL SEVERE POTENTIAL DOES NOT AT THIS TIME APPEAR TO WARRANT SLIGHT RISK UPGRADE. ..GOSS/GRAMS.. 08/09/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A MEAN MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP OVER THE GREAT LAKES/NE STATES AS AN INITIAL SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTS EWD FROM OH ACROSS PA/SRN NEW ENGLAND...AND AN UPSTREAM WAVE MOVES ESEWD OVER THE UPPER GREAT LAKES. AT THE SURFACE...A LOW INVOF LAKE ERIE WILL PROGRESS EWD/ENEWD ACROSS NRN PA/WRN NY TO NRN NY/NRN NEW ENGLAND BY TONIGHT...WHILE A TRAILING COLD FRONT MOVES EWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. THE WRN EXTENT OF THIS FRONT HAS BEEN REINFORCED BY MULTIPLE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS...AND HAS STALLED ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN AR AND OK. FARTHER W...A SEPARATE SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER ID WILL MOVE EWD OVER WY AND THEN ESEWD OVER THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS LATE TODAY INTO TONIGHT. AN ASSOCIATED LEE CYCLONE IS EXPECTED TO FORM THIS AFTERNOON INVOF NE CO ALONG THE TRAILING PORTION OF THE COLD FRONTAL SURGE ASSOCIATED WITH THE UPPER GREAT LAKES TROUGH...AND THEN DEVELOP SEWD OVERNIGHT TOWARD NW OK.

sections.title: CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: THE RICHEST LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IS INITIALLY TIED TO THE OUTFLOW REINFORCED FRONT ACROSS OK/AR...THOUGH RESIDUAL DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S ACROSS KS WILL SPREAD NWWD LATER TODAY INTO SW NEB. THIS MOISTURE...IN COMBINATION WITH DAYTIME HEATING AND MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AOA 7 C/KM...WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES NEAR 2000 J/KG. ADDITIONALLY...DEEP-LAYER AND LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL INCREASE WITH THE APPROACH OF THE WY SHORTWAVE TROUGH...RESULTING IN AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE MAIN INITIAL THREAT THIS AFTERNOON FROM ERN WY INTO WRN NEB WITH THE MORE DISCRETE STORMS...WHILE THE DAMAGING WIND THREAT SHOULD INCREASE THIS EVENING AS STORMS COALESCE INTO ONE OR MORE CLUSTERS WHILE MOVING SEWD INTO NW KS.

sections.title: MS/AL/GA AREA THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A SERIES OF CONVECTIVELY-ENHANCED MIDLEVEL TROUGHS WILL CONTINUE ESEWD FROM NW AR AND NRN MS TO AL/GA TODAY...WHILE THE SRN EXTENT OF THE OH VALLEY TROUGH BRUSHES THE SRN APPALACHIANS. THE ACCOMPANYING SURFACE COLD FRONT WILL LIKEWISE MOVE SEWD ACROSS THE SRN APPALACHIANS AND NRN GA/AL/MS THIS AFTERNOON. THE PRESENCE OF LOW-MID 70S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS AND DIFFERENTIAL HEATING ALONG THE RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS NRN MS/AL WILL SUPPORT MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG IN AN ENVIRONMENT WITH MODEST WNWLY MIDLEVEL FLOW. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP FROM THE REMNANTS OF THE MORNING MS/AL CONVECTION...AND FARTHER NE ALONG THE SYNOPTIC COLD FRONT THIS AFTERNOON INVOF THE SRN APPALACHIANS. THE COMBINATION OF MODERATE INSTABILITY AND VERTICAL SHEAR WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS WITH THE PRIMARY RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING.

sections.title: ERN PA/NY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: IN ADVANCE OF THE OH SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND SURFACE LOW...A SURFACE WARM FRONT WILL MOVE SLOWLY NWD FROM ERN PA INTO NY...WHILE REMAINING QUASI-STATIONARY NEAR THE SRN NEW ENGLAND COAST. THIS WILL ALLOW BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S TO SPREAD NWD...THOUGH THE MAGNITUDE OF WARM SECTOR INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON WILL BE LIMITED BY MODEST SURFACE HEATING AND POOR MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. AN INCREASE IN VERTICAL SHEAR WITH THE APPROACH OF THE MIDLEVEL TROUGH COULD RESULT IN SOME RISK FOR ORGANIZED THUNDERSTORMS...THOUGH THE WEAK BUOYANCY/LAPSE RATES WILL TEMPER THE RISK OF SEVERE STORMS.

sections.title: LOWER MI/INDIANA/OH THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: THE UPPER GREAT LAKES TROUGH AND ITS ASSOCIATED SECONDARY FRONTAL SURGE WILL MOVE SEWD FROM WI/IL THIS MORNING TO LOWER MI/INDIANA/NW OH BY THIS EVENING. RESIDUAL BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S AND SURFACE HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS WILL ALLOW THE DEVELOPMENT OF WEAK-MODERATE INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON IN ADVANCE OF THE FRONT. DEEP-LAYER SPEED SHEAR WILL ALSO INCREASE...RESULTING IN AN ENVIRONMENT WITH SOME POTENTIAL TO SUPPORT ORGANIZED STRONG/SEVERE STORMS. HOWEVER...FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL LARGELY BE LIMITED TO THE SOMEWHAT DIFFUSE COLD FRONT...AND STORM COVERAGE SHOULD REMAIN SOMEWHAT ISOLATED. GIVEN THAT THE CONDITIONAL HAIL/WIND RISK IS NOT PARTICULARLY HIGH...WILL MAINTAIN ONLY LOW HAIL/WIND PROBABILITIES. ..THOMPSON/ROGERS.. 08/09/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM CENTRAL IL INTO OH
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE DELMARVA REGION NORTHWARD INTO SOUTHWEST NEW ENGLAND... BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW REMAINS OVER THE CENTRAL AND EASTERN UNITED STATES TODAY WITH AT LEAST MODEST WESTERLY FLOW AS FAR SOUTH AS THE TN VALLEY AND MID ATLANTIC STATES. THIS FLOW REGIME WILL POSE A RISK FOR AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS OVER SEVERAL PARTS OF THE NATION TODAY.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A MID LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER MT. THIS FEATURE IS PROGD BY 12Z MODEL RUNS TO TRACK SOUTHEASTWARD INTO THE NORTHERN PLAINS THIS EVENING. INCREASING LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL SPREAD INTO THE PORTIONS OF WY AND WESTERN SD/NEB BY LATE AFTERNOON...HELPING TO INITIATE SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS. STORMS CURRENTLY AFFECTING THIS REGION MAY LEAD TO OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES THAT FURTHER FOCUS INITIATION. RATHER STRONG EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL FAVOR DISCRETE SUPERCELL STORM MODE WITH VERY LARGE HAIL POSSIBLE IN THE STRONGER CELLS. STORMS WILL MOVE/DEVELOP SOUTHEASTWARD AND AFFECT PARTS OF NORTHEAST CO AND WESTERN KS DURING THE EVENING...WHERE MORE UPSCALE ORGANIZATION INTO AN MCS IS POSSIBLE SUGGESTING A GREATER THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: THE COLLECTIVE OUTFLOW FROM YESTERDAYS CONVECTION EXTENDS FROM SOUTHERN AR ACROSS MS/AL INTO NORTHWEST GA. STRONG HEATING WILL OCCUR AHEAD OF THE BOUNDARY...WHERE STEEP LAPSE RATES AND MODERATE-STRONG INSTABILITY WILL DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON. MODELS VARY ON THE COVERAGE OF CONVECTION LATER TODAY. HOWEVER...SUFFICIENT NORTHWESTERLY FLOW ALOFT WILL SUPPORT A RISK OF SCATTERED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS ALONG A CORRIDOR FROM NORTHERN LA INTO NORTH GA AND UPSTATE SC.

sections.title: IL/IND/OH
sections.text: A RATHER STRONG SURFACE COLD FRONT IS SAGGING SOUTHWARD ACROSS NORTHERN IL AND INTO WESTERN LOWER MI. RESIDUAL DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S AND COOLING TEMPERATURES ALOFT...COUPLED WITH FULL SUNSHINE...WILL YIELD AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES AROUND 1500 J/KG AND STEEP LAPSE RATES. MOST MODELS SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A LINE OF CONVECTION FROM CENTRAL IL...ACROSS IND...INTO OH BY LATE AFTERNOON. THE ENVIRONMENT IN THIS REGION WOULD SUPPORT A RISK OF HAIL AND GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS IN THE STRONGER CELLS.

sections.title: DELMARVA TO SOUTHWEST NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: A RATHER STRONG SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS ROTATING EASTWARD ACROSS NY/PA THIS MORNING. WIDESPREAD CLOUDS AHEAD OF THIS TROUGH HAVE LIMITED DAYTIME HEATING IN THE WARM SECTOR...OVER PARTS OF NY/PA/NY/DE. HOWEVER...CLEARING SKIES ARE EXPECTED TO OVERSPREAD THE REGION THIS AFTERNOON ALLOWING A FEW HOURS OF HEATING. MODELS ARE IN GENERAL AGREEMENT THAT SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS THIS REGION BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW FAVORABLE VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES FOR ORGANIZED OR EVEN SUPERCELL STORM STRUCTURES. THE MAIN UNCERTAINTY REMAINS THE DEGREE OF DESTABILIZATION THAT WILL OCCUR. THERE APPEARS TO BE SUFFICIENT RISK TO INTRODUCE A SMALL SLIGHT RISK IN THIS AREA. LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WOULD BE POSSIBLE IN THE STRONGER AND MORE ORGANIZED CELLS. ..HART/HURLBUT.. 08/09/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OH/INDIANA AND VICINITY
sections.text: ...CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS SEWD INTO OK AND THE TX PNHDL... SEVERAL AREAS OF SEVERE CONVECTION ARE ONGOING ATTM...INCLUDING ERN WY AND THE WRN NEB PANHANDLE...SWRN NEB SWD INTO KS...AND THE TX/OH PANHANDLE REGION. STORMS ARE ONGOING WITHIN AN AREA OF FAVORABLE INSTABILITY/SHEAR... WITH SHEAR EXPECTED TO FURTHER INCREASE AS SELY LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS THIS EVENING. THE INCREASING LOW-LEVEL JET WILL ALSO SUPPORT A CONTINUATION OF THE STORMS AND ASSOCIATED SEVERE THREAT THROUGH THE EVENING AND INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS...AS CONVECTION SHIFTS GENERALLY SEWD ACROSS KS AND INTO OK. ALONG WITH POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL -- ESPECIALLY IN THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS...DAMAGING WINDS AND AN ISOLATED TORNADO OR TWO REMAIN POSSIBLE. GREATEST TORNADO POTENTIAL SHOULD REMAIN ACROSS NEB AND NWRN KS...WHERE LOWER LCLS AND GREATER LOW-LEVEL SHEAR EXIST.

sections.title: THE MIDWEST
sections.text: BAND OF STORMS MOVING SEWD ACROSS OH AND INDIANA ATTM IS PROGGED TO SLOWLY WEAKEN OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS AS AIRMASS DIURNALLY COOLS/STABILIZES. UNTIL THEN...MODEST INSTABILITY AND MODERATE DEEP-LAYER NWLYS WILL SUPPORT LOCALLY DAMAGING GUSTS AND POSSIBLY HAIL WITH STRONGER STORMS.

sections.title: THE GULF COAST AREA
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DIMINISH IN INTENSITY OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH THE LOSS OF DIURNAL HEATING. STILL...LOCALLY DAMAGING GUSTS MAY OCCUR WITH STRONGER PORTIONS OF THE SWD-MOVING BAND OF CONVECTION. ..GOSS.. 08/10/2011
